body:
Hi Justin,

I spent some time on roofrepairtyler.com this week. Your repair-first approach is genuinely refreshing, but the homepage makes people work too hard to find it. The FAQ section shows up before your services are ever presented, there is no actual services section on the page, and the same free estimate form appears twice in one long scroll, with repeated call-to-action blocks in between. A homeowner with an active leak has to wade through all of that before they can even see what you do.

So I redesigned your homepage, and the PDF is attached to this email. Your services now get their own clear section up top, there is one simple estimate form, and your 5.0 rating from 27 Google reviews sits right where a nervous homeowner can see it.

Roofing sites are a big part of my work. I built Leal Roofing (leal-roofing.com) with clear service pages and an easy quote flow. I also built Severe Weather Roofing (severeweatherroofing.com), focused on storm damage work where people need help fast.

If you like the direction, I can put it on your real domain and build out the rest of the site. If not, keep the PDF as free ideas, no hard feelings either way.

Best,
Hassan
name: Tyler Roof Repair
subject: 🏠 Two estimate forms on one page, but your services hide in the footer
